analysis:
The only change is a documentation addition to docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 2172-2184) describing Flint constrained-decode chaining: FlintNativeProtocolConstraint and FlintAnswerStopConstraint opt into CBv2 constrained chaining, with a mask cache keyed by constraint state. The paragraph also says RecursiveSI/flint-int4 is on the automatic paged list and starts at legacy serving width on M5 Pro/Max/Ultra. I examined both base units, covering lines 1629-2248, and the patch. There is no code, protocol, key-handling, attestation, cache-storage or authorization change.

No threat-model regression is evident. The mask cache is keyed by constraint state while output budget remains, which is a performance optimization that does not touch the T-041 prefix-cache surface (SSD tier, HMAC lookup tags, cacheSalt). The doc states that token output is identical to unchained decode. That is a correctness claim by the doc, and the underlying Swift and SDK implementation was not supplied, so it is unverified here.

Open integration questions for the source change, if one exists elsewhere: (1) whether the redraw-on-state-change path restores per-row RNG and penalty state without leaking cross-request state (T-028 residual GPU data); (2) whether the cached device mask is keyed per request or shared across tenants. A state-only key should be tenant-independent, but this was not verified. (3) Whether the paged-list addition for flint-int4 changes the prefix-cache or KV memory-admission paths. The doc says it is a width default only. None of these can be confirmed from a docs-only diff, so they are noted as unverified contracts rather than findings.
